lists, counts, search and cursors show the caller tenant only; a cursor of another tenant is refused like a garbled one
scope(tenant) opens one tenant and the tripwire sees exactly that tenant for every operation of the handle
the same id means a different object in each tenant; counters, ordering and quotas are per tenant
ids stay in numeric order past four digits and a page after proj-9999 starts at proj-10000
list, search and pages: counts and cursors are the tenant's own, search is case-insensitive substring, the page tail is exact
cursors and ETags are keyed MACs over the tenant (and the query): a value of one tenant verifies in no other, and any altered character fails
answers are frozen copies: nothing a consumer does reaches the store
the audit trail: a ring per user of a tenant, a sequence per tenant, a separate bounded anonymous ring
the snapshot is a copy: resources and counters as plain data, audit excluded from the tenants
the default randomness and no tripwire: two stores have different keys and scope() needs no observer
the audit trail is per tenant: a denial or a probe is recorded in the caller tenant only, anonymous refusals in no tenant
one user flooding denials cannot evict the record of another user or of another tenant
quota exhaustion in one tenant starves nobody else: projects and sessions
mass assignment: a body can never set a role, a tenant, an owner, an id or a version; the owner is the verified user
a token altered in any ONE character, or of any other shape, is refused; the original keeps working
two credentials, a lowercase scheme and an empty value are handled by one strict rule
a user that belongs to no tenant, and a member of ANOTHER tenant, cannot redeem a ticket for it
record and recordAnonymous return the stored entry: frozen, numbered, with the user
two users of two tenants: every probe is answered as specified and the verdict is derived from facts
the DOM invariants hold after a run: unique ids, a row per check, a single live status, the button enabled again
a tenant with nothing to compare is handled: an empty tenant, no foreign-only ids, no profiles
bad input: no token or a malformed one sends nothing; two tokens of the SAME tenant cannot be compared
a forged answer is never shown as isolated or allowed (a leak, a status and code that disagree, a failing network, a 304, a wrong count)
the run is bound: a second click while a run is in flight is ignored, the timeout signal is used when the platform has one
page.js asks only for ids that index.html declares, and never for another element
the child serves a prepared world and a positive control keeps its connection open

anonymous to authenticated: the session id AND the token change at login, and the anonymous token is dead (no fixation)
a client can neither choose nor adopt a session id: a body naming one is refused, a header or cookie is not an identity channel, a refusal consumes nothing
a login ticket is ONE-TIME: replay, expiry, an unknown or malformed ticket and a session token as a ticket are all TICKET_INVALID
an authenticated session cannot log in again (that would be a tenant switch without logging out): 409 and the ticket stays unspent
logout ends the session for good: the dead token is refused everywhere, a second logout too, and a new login is a new session
an admin revokes by session id or by user: the token is refused at once; revoking what already ended is a refusal
a session expires by the injected clock and never revives; the state an admin sees is derived, not written by a refused request
tenant switch needs a fresh authentication: a request, a claim, or the old token never moves a session; a new login is a separate session
every illegal transition is a typed refusal with NO effect on the world
identity: revoking dana in one tenant ends her sessions of that tenant only, in both directions, and an empty revoke ends nothing anywhere
identity: a user of the other tenant, and a user of no tenant, is "not found" and ends nothing
identity: a session id of the other tenant is "not found", identical to an id that never existed, in both directions
identity: a role change names a tenant's membership: dana is a member in alder and a viewer in birch, and each change leaves the other tenant's role alone
identity: the last admin of a tenant stays, whatever admins the other tenants have (a second admin elsewhere is no second admin here)
identity: the session list of a tenant holds that tenant's sessions, in the order they were made, and the same user name appears in both lists with different ids
identity: a tenant's session quota and record bound count that tenant's sessions only, in both directions
identity: an ended record is dropped from ITS OWN tenant when the record bound is met, never from another tenant
service: the audit of a tenant holds that tenant's own decisions about dana and nobody else's, in both directions
service: a revoke by user names the verified admin's own tenant, whatever user name the body carries (both directions, effect and answer)
HTTP: the alder admin revokes "dana": her alder session ends, her birch session answers, and birch's own session list still says active
HTTP (mirror): the birch admin revokes "dana": her birch session ends, her alder session answers and alder's own list still says active
HTTP: dana with two sessions in alder and one in birch: the alder revoke ends exactly two, a repeated revoke ends none, the birch session never changes
HTTP: a revoke by session id of the other tenant is the answer for an id that never existed, in both directions, and ends nothing
HTTP: a revoke of "dana" by the admin of a tenant she is no member of is "not found" and ends nothing
HTTP: logging dana out of one tenant leaves her session of the other tenant live, in both directions
HTTP: a role change by one tenant's admin changes dana's role in that tenant only, in both directions (and what each role may do follows)
HTTP: each tenant's admin session list holds its own sessions of dana and the other tenant's are not in it (and the counts agree)
HTTP: the audit trail of a tenant holds that tenant's decisions about dana and the other tenant's are not in it (both directions)
HTTP: session quotas and ended records are per tenant: a full tenant refuses, the other tenant still serves, and eviction never reaches across
HTTP: the same project id in two tenants is two projects: updating or deleting it in one never touches the other (both directions)
every refusal code of the closed table has a row, and each row carries the status of its code
the Node-own rows are exactly the answers Node gives itself: unknown Expect, parse error, oversized header, CONNECT
a request whose connection was ended while its body was read has no effect and no audit entry, even for a body that is invalid
a valid mutation whose connection was ended while it waited for the commit queue never commits
login with a malformed credential is refused TOKEN_MALFORMED, spends nothing, and the same ticket then logs in
every route that requires a credential refuses a malformed one TOKEN_MALFORMED
the route that creates an anonymous session reads no credential: a malformed header is not an error there
a well-formed credential in any case of the scheme is read: bearer, BEARER and Bearer all authenticate
a role change takes effect at once on EXISTING tokens in both directions; downgrade then re-upgrade is decided by the current role only
the last admin of a tenant cannot be demoted; with a second admin the first may step down
a revoked user's in-flight request has no effect: revoke, logout and a role downgrade between the decision and the commit
the decision is repeated at the commit: a hook between the first decision and the effect that expires the session leaves no effect
concurrent logins with ONE ticket: exactly one wins, and exactly one session exists
a login racing a logout and a revoke of the same user leaves every token in exactly one legal state, whatever the arrival order
